Page 1 • All About Me & Academic Biography

Hello, I'm Adnan Topdemir.

I am a Third-year undergraduate student in the Department of Foreign Language Education (English Language Teaching). My academic curiosity consists but are not limited to sociolinguistics, critical discourse analysis, and the pedagogical potential of interactive storytelling.

Throughout my undergraduate studies, I have explored how both classical literary texts—ranging from William Shakespeare's The Tempest and Aphra Behn's Oroonoko to Romantic poetry—and modern collaborative media and hobbies such as how tabletop role-playing games (TTRPGs) can lower the affective filter and cultivate authentic communicative competence in English as a Foreign Language (EFL) classrooms.

1. Creative Non-Fiction Final project: Telling of a very personal story of mine using the Creative Non-Fiction storytelling strategies.

2. EFL 254 Communicative Lesson Plan Summary (50 Minutes | CEFR B2):

• Objective: Learners negotiate solutions to a collaborative scenario using modal verbs of deduction and conditionals.

• Pre-Task (10 min): Visual schema activation and lexical scaffolding.

• While-Task (25 min): Group role-play with asymmetric specialist cards requiring authentic information-gap communication.

• Post-Task (15 min): Reflective debriefing and delayed communicative error correction.

Page 3 • Voluntary Campus Involvement, Academic Interests & Hobbies

Community Service & My Interests

Combining campus community workshops, tabletop collaborative storytelling, miniature scale modeling, and speculative literature.

Community Service

University Fantasy Fiction Society Workshops

As an active member and current president of our university's Fantasy Fiction Society (Fantastik Kurgu Topluluğu), I help organize welcoming student events and delivered a 20-minute seminar introducing Tabletop Role-Playing Games (TTRPGs) and their cognitive, social, and linguistic benefits.

Academic & Creative Interest

Collaborative Storytelling & Worldbuilding

I design narrative campaigns and historical-fantasy settings across systems like D&D 3.5e, Mythic Iceland (BRP), and Pathfinder. Crafting lore and regional dialects directly enriches my research into sociolinguistics and interactive EFL speaking tasks.

Hobby & Craft

Miniature Scale Modeling & Speculative Fiction

I assemble and paint finely detailed scale miniatures (such as Warhammer 40,000 and Age of Sigmar models), practicing patience and color theory, alongside reading Ursula K. Le Guin's Earthsea cycle and Joe Abercrombie's novels.

My Thoughts, Reflections & Note to Self

Click any blog entry to edit its title or paragraphs directly, or publish a new reflection post below.

Pedagogical Reflection Published by Adnan Topdemir • 2025–2026 Academic Year

1. Lowering the Affective Filter Through Collaborative Storytelling

While preparing my 20-minute presentation for our university's Fantasy Fiction Society on the cognitive and social benefits of Tabletop Role-Playing Games (TTRPGs), I kept connecting those mechanics with our discussions in ELT Methodology II (EFL254). In many language classrooms, speaking anxiety—what Stephen Krashen calls a high affective filter—prevents students from taking communicative risks. Stepping into a role-play persona gives learners a safe narrative mask where communication becomes purposeful and collaborative.

Note to Self Personal Academic Memo

2. Note to Self: Patience in Craft, Research, and Teaching

Whether I am analyzing colonial discourse in Shakespeare's The Tempest, examining sociolinguistic registers in the Forgotten Realms, or painting a scale Warhammer miniature under a desk lamp, meaningful work rewards patience and layered preparation. You cannot rush a basecoat paint any more than you can rush a learner's development in a second language.
